summary: Chunk 2 (units 42-82) is carefully done: no wrong plant identification found (all hedged or tagged; pūtīkarañja, śaṭhī correctly left disputed; kuṣṭha=costus, kramuka=areca, trivṛt, pathyā, bṛhatī-pair, punarnavā all acceptable). Real problems: an added 'or'/या in 69; conjectural readings used silently in the translation in 66 (devāhva) and 82 (kola, bṛhatī); glossary-form fixes (siddha=पकाया, śūla=pain, no added गति/हों/है, 'appears to complete'). Open for the owner: 47 (vṛttitasya conjecture and Hindi आचरण), 48 (flag contradicts metre; kurvan vs kurvanto), 53 (probably ā + klamanāśāt, not a noun āklama; vyajet is a plain pot. of vi-√aj), 75 (pakvaloṣṭa; madhuka vs madhūka), 79 (avipravṛtta), 62 (case of kalkam). The 10 text_flags are all plausible except 48 (weak). 49: a- governing all three is a fair reading, stated as unsure. No regrouping needed (67 holds two half-verses on one line).
glossary_suggestions: Conjectural readings: when `words` use a corrected form that changes a drug name (66 devāhva, 82 kola/bṛhatī), the translation says 'on a conjectural reading' (Hindi: अनुमानित पाठ), no brackets in Hindi.

Hindi sthirā/śālaparṇī = सरिवन; Hindi varṣābhū = पुनर्नवा, जिसे गदहपूर्णा कहते हैं; bṛhatī = बनभंटा, kaṇṭakārī = भटकटैया; rohiṣa = रूसा घास (Cymbopogon martinii, probable); trivṛt = निशोथ; pathyā = हरड़; kuṣṭha (drug) = कूठ (Saussurea costus, standard); kramuka = सुपारी (probable).
Lists with ati- or a- before several members: do not add 'or'/'and' (69); ati-/a- scope noted in notes.
vyajet = pot. of vi-√aj (to fan); ā + ablative = 'up to' (53, if the owner accepts the split).
bilva: consider 'bael (Aegle marmelos)' instead of 'wood-apple', which is also used for Limonia acidissima; keep one rendering book-wide.
OPEN: rendering of 'ānulomika/anulomayet' (Hindi स्वाभाविक दिशा के अनुसार used in ch06 chunk 1; English 'natural direction').
